facts.statement: The genus Palaealectoris is classified under the parent group Tetraonidae.
Fossils of Palaealectoris have been found in Nebraska and Maryland and date to the Early Miocene.
facts.quote: Its fossilized remains, found in the Marsland Formation, a part of the Agate Fossil Beds National Monument in Nebraska, and in the Calvert Formation in Maryland, are dated from the Early Miocene.

facts.statement: Palaealectoris lived between 23.1 and 18.5 million years ago during the Chattian to Burdigalian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Burdigalian (23.1 to 18.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: A fragmentary tibiotarsus was collected in May 1925 near Chesapeake Beach, Maryland, by Remington Kellogg and Norman Boss.
facts.quote: The first remains associated with the genus, a fragmentary tibiotarsus, were collected in May 1925 in marine strata belonging to the Miocene-aged Calvert Formation, near Chesapeake Beach, Maryland, by Remington Kellogg and Norman Boss.

facts.statement: The holotype remains were collected in the summer of 1928 by Erich Maren Schlaikjer in Nebraska.
facts.quote: The holotype remains of Palaealectoris were collected during the summer of 1928 by Erich Maren Schlaikjer in Lower Miocene deposits belonging to the Agate Fossil Beds in Sioux County, Nebraska.

facts.statement: The genus was described in 1930 by Alexander Wetmore based on parts of a left humerus.
facts.quote: The genus was first described shortly after, in 1930, by Alexander Wetmore, at Schlaikjer's demand, based on the two extremities of a left humerus, with P. incertus as the type species.

facts.statement: The superior crest of the humerus showed similarities to chachalacas, likely representing a convergent adaptation.
facts.quote: The superior crest of the humerus shared several similarities in development with that of the chachalacas, although this was probably a convergent adaptation.
